added_failure_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm (its gate is a measurement script, not a suite), so there is no baseline/after pair to difference; the zero is the neutral value the record shape requires, not a measurement. I re-ran the named gate at the head it read and it exited 0.

findings.text: the caption places the eps-squared model branch "on the left" and the rounding branch "on the right", but the plotted axis runs 1e-8 (left) to 1e-2 (right), so the model branch is the right-hand one and the rounding branch the left, and the same sentence's "one to two decades above the line" understates the measured 2.1 to 2.8 decades; a reader following the caption looks at the wrong branch of the only figure the decision carries.

the fragment says "the kernel's own arithmetic is exact to double-double", but no double-double arithmetic exists anywhere in nova (grep for double-double, longdouble and float128 over nova/ returns nothing and nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py works in float64), so the sentence attributes the measured rounding branch to a mechanism that is not there, though the conclusion is unaffected because plain double rounding is at least as large.

the fragment cites an "independent 80-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature" as the control that caught the swapped target/source argument order, but no such control is in the landed tree (scripts/edge_sheet holds only reference, sweep, verify and figure), so a reader cannot re-run the check the reference's validity rests on.

the gate iterates whatever slopes and targets the receipt happens to hold and asserts neither the fixed five slopes, twelve targets and thirteen widths that the done_when fixes nor that a non-converging target was reported rather than dropped, so a receipt that lost a slope or a target still prints EXIT=0.

save_checked re-implements a helper the repository already carries at scripts/prototypes/bank_solve_profile/plot.py:45 and scripts/prototypes/bank_solve_driver/plot.py:28, and the prototype also declares the 31.1x16 cm canvas this copy omits, so a third copy means the next restyle fixes none of them together.
